newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares held back by ENI, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares held back by ENI, end lower.

text.p: This weekend's pricing of a second tranche of shares in state-controlled energy giant ENI held back sentiment in lacklustre day on Friday.
Shares drifted lower, but managed a late rally in afternoon trade after an improvement in bonds, lira and bunds and U.S. data which the market considered to be positive.
The Mibtel all-share index finished 0.25 percent easier at 9,827 while the blue-chip Mib-30 index ended 0.34 percent weaker at 14,783.

ENI finished the day 1.81 percent off at 7,170. The Treasury said last week private buyers would have at least a 3.5 percent price discount to today's closing level and set the top price range at which shares would be offered to private invetors at 7,425 lire.
Treausury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was due to hold a news conference on Saturday to discuss pricing details.
The Treasury said on Thursday it was increasing the total number of ENI shares offered for sale to 1.1 billion from 700 million.

"The market has really been held back by ENI," said one dealer. "We've seen some international institutional investors who are reasonably sure they will be getting their allocations pre-selling in anticipation of the new shares."
The Milan market shed more than one percent at midsession. But dealers noted greater optimism on 1997 budget following deals on income and regional taxes.
The leader of hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which holds balance of power in the lower house of parliament, also said its support for the package was assured.

Pirelli sank again in the wake of disappointing tyre data which pointed to lower margins. It ended the day 1.88 percent off at 2,659. Dealers also noted profit-taking and investors switching out of the stock and into other industrials.
Ambroveneto finished 4.62 percent up at 3,284 ahead of Tuesday's board meeting at which the market is wondering whether the company could decide to make bid for Banco di Napoli.
